source.notes: ADR-238's compiled predicate list against the alignments display's hand-written read test, the default flag exclusion (unmapped, QC-failed, duplicate) plus a MAPQ floor of 20, over two million BAM-shaped records, arms interleaved in one process, min of 15 rounds, on ada. The first compiler (a closure per flag bit, a coercion per compare, Array.every) measured 5.5x on the laptop; the fused compiler (one mask compare for the flag bits, a typed number bound, an unrolled list, lanes over the record in hand) is the row below. For scale, @gmod/bam 10.0.1 fetches, inflates and decodes a volvox read in 359 ns on ada before any extraction, so the remaining gap is about 0.6% of decode alone. The whole-fetch rows are ADR-240 step 3a's gate (node --experimental-transform-types plugins/alignments/benches/readFilterFetch.bench.ts --rounds=15, measured 2026-10-22): 1000x.shortread.bam chr22_mask:124000-143000 opened afresh each round, 153,677 records, the same four entries per record, on ada; a second run read 129.7 and 127.5 ms. The list costs nothing measurable there, so the worker runs it. The display rows are ADR-240 step 3's other displays, measured 2026-10-22 on the laptop on AC power. Variant site test (node plugins/variants/benches/siteFilter.bench.ts --rounds=15): the 1000 Genomes chr1 slice, 1342 records x 2504 samples, a MAF floor of 0.01 and a missingness ceiling of 0.1; the test alone runs 100 passes over the precomputed allele summaries, about 16 ns a site, and the whole path counts alleles first, which is the cost a fetch pays. Feature filter chain (node packages/core/benches/filterChain.bench.ts --rounds=25 --features=200000): one expression over 200,000 SimpleFeatures through SerializableFilterChain; the hand column is the chain as it stood before the list, and three runs spread 200-300 ns a feature for both the old chain and an expression entry, so they are one cost. The field-test row runs the same filter as `{ field: 'score', gt: 5 }` with no jexl.
